notes.content: (120 UNITS) The Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology ( Link ) provides a broad, comprehensive study of physical activity and human movement. Students observe and study movement across the lifespan from mechanical, physiological, psychological, sociocultural, behavioral, instructional and professional points of view. Focused concentration areas provide additional background knowledge and preparation for advanced study or professional careers in allied health and medicine, exercise science, gerokinesiology, physical education, recreation and physical activity promotion, sport studies, and strength and conditioning.. All courses in the major, including prerequisites, must be completed with a “C” (2.0) or better, and must be taken on an Option 1 (letter grade) basis. Kinesiology courses with the “junior or senior standing” prerequisite require students to have completed a minimum of 55 units. Intercollegiate sport courses may be completed with the Credit/No Credit option. Human Anatomy & Physiology (3 to 4 units) Performance Courses (6 units) - At least 1 course from*: -Aquatics -Individual Physical Activities -Group Physical Activities Requirements for Major (30 units) Concentration (21 units) Concentration The Pre-Allied Health concentration ( Link ) provides advanced scientific background and applied knowledge for Kinesiology majors who are interested in entering advanced graduate degree programs in athletic training, occupational therapy, physical therapy, physician assistant or other allied health fields. It also allows students to meet some of the prerequisite requirements for advanced graduate allied health degree programs. Since each graduate degree program has unique prerequisite requirements, it is highly recommended that students seek academic advising prior to declaring the concentration. In addition to the requirements for the major, students must meet all other university requirements for a bachelor’s degree. Please consult the Graduation Requirements for the Bachelor’s Degree section in this catalog for complete information.
notes.contentHtml:
(120 UNITS)

The Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology (Link) provides a broad, comprehensive study of physical activity and human movement. Students observe and study movement across the lifespan from mechanical, physiological, psychological, sociocultural, behavioral, instructional and professional points of view. Focused concentration areas provide additional background knowledge and preparation for advanced study or professional careers in allied health and medicine, exercise science, gerokinesiology, physical education, recreation and physical activity promotion, sport studies, and strength and conditioning..

All courses in the major, including prerequisites, must be completed with a “C” (2.0) or better, and must be taken on an Option 1 (letter grade) basis. Kinesiology courses with the “junior or senior standing” prerequisite require students to have completed a minimum of 55 units. Intercollegiate sport courses may be completed with the Credit/No Credit option.

  • Human Anatomy & Physiology (3 to 4 units)
  • Performance Courses (6 units) - At least 1 course from*:
    • -Aquatics
    • -Individual Physical Activities
    • -Group Physical Activities
  • Requirements for Major (30 units)
  • Concentration (21 units)

Concentration

The Pre-Allied Health concentration (Link) provides advanced scientific background and applied knowledge for Kinesiology majors who are interested in entering advanced graduate degree programs in athletic training, occupational therapy, physical therapy, physician assistant or other allied health fields. It also allows students to meet some of the prerequisite requirements for advanced graduate allied health degree programs. Since each graduate degree program has unique prerequisite requirements, it is highly recommended that students seek academic advising prior to declaring the concentration.

In addition to the requirements for the major, students must meet all other university requirements for a bachelor’s degree. Please consult the Graduation Requirements for the Bachelor’s Degree section in this catalog for complete information.
